Contemporary coverage heard similarities to Hi-NRG and documented fast disco in early Chicago sets. House drew on several dance-floor traditions.

House and garage-house grew from DJ practices that reworked disco, but scholarship cautions against a simple, inevitable evolution: Chicago house also formed through Black, queer, and Latino social worlds and new production practices. “Derived from disco” is a lineage shorthand, not a complete origin account.

Massive Attack are principally described as trip-hop pioneers; their catalog includes downtempo and ambient-associated qualities, but “downtempo” is broad and less central than trip-hop. Medium is more defensible than high.

AllMusic describes the Bristol group as trip-hop pioneers; scholarship cautions that the genre label is contested and sometimes rejected by Bristol artists. Central association stands. Correct the graph’s current AllMusic URL, which appears to identify a different artist record.

Ravel is often grouped with musical Impressionism, but the label is disputed and he resisted a simple movement classification. The edge is useful with this qualification; high overstates taxonomic certainty.
Norwegian reference and label biographies identify Mayhem as foundational to Norwegian black metal. The band is a central representative, while the wider genre’s origins remain multi-source.
Megadeth is routinely grouped with the foundational thrash “Big Four”; AllMusic calls the band a thrash-metal institution. Strong core association.
Institutional sources identify Mei as a master and major innovator of Peking opera. This is a defining association, not merely a performer credit.
Rock Hall calls the early work raw, breakneck thrash; Oxford scholarship describes Metallica as pioneering the style. Their later catalog broadens, but the foundational thrash association is strong.
Rock Hall says Jackson redefined pop and names him the King of Pop. The edge is central despite his work crossing soul, funk, disco, and R&B.
NALIS documents his breakthrough as calypso became widely recorded; Smithsonian identifies him as “Calypso King.” A defining calypsonian.
GRAMMY documents a Best Merengue Album award; congressional text and her official biography call her the Queen of Merengue. Strong representative association.
AllMusic calls Ministry one of the leaders/founders of industrial metal; AP places the group before the style’s mainstream spread. Strong central fit, though its earliest synth-pop phase differs.
Muraoka was a shakuhachi player (not a gagaku instrument); the link rests on the crossover album Gagaku and Beyond with Herbie Mann, not on court-music practice.
Her own biography calls her an electroclash pioneer; contemporary coverage places her at the center of the movement. High confidence.
Reference and scholarship explicitly situate Mogwai among post-rock’s defining Scottish bands. Strong central association.
Morbid Angel is consistently identified as a pioneering and defining Florida death-metal band. Strong genre-central fit.

Motorbass describes itself as an early French Touch band; scholarly and French press histories place the duo’s *Pansoul* among foundational French house records. High association, with the scene’s broader influences understood.
Reference classification includes MBV among dream-pop artists; scholarship addresses the band’s distinctive pop/noise aesthetic. Dream pop is one valid lens among shoegaze/noise-pop labels.
MBV are widely recognized as architects of shoegaze, with *Loveless* central to the style’s history. Strong defining association.
*Illmatic* is a canonical Queens boom-bap album, but boom bap describes a production lineage more directly than Nas’s entire career. Keep medium, scoped to the classic 1990s work.

AllMusic calls Neon Indian one of chillwave’s definitive late-2000s acts; scholarship situates the project within the scene. Note Palomo’s discomfort with the tag, but its representative value remains clear.

AP identifies New Edition as performing New Jack Swing material; the style is strongly associated with the group’s later period and Bobby Brown, but Teddy Riley/Guy and other acts are more directly identified as architects. Medium suits an important representative association, not originator status.

Academic writing includes Nine Inch Nails among industrial-metal performers, and the category is supported. The band is more consistently framed as industrial rock/industrial music; the genre edge is valid but not as defining as its industrial-rock association.
Rock Hall explicitly describes *Nevermind*’s grunge sound and the band’s Pacific Northwest impact. Nirvana is a defining grunge act.
Contemporary coverage calls him the world’s pre-eminent qawwali performer; museum and specialist sources describe his qawwali lineage and international influence. This is a defining association.

Rock Hall says N.W.A. solidified gangsta rap; LOC calls *Straight Outta Compton* its standard bearer. The group’s centrality is well established, while recognizing earlier contributors such as Schoolly D and Ice-T.
Sources establish N.W.A.’s Compton/Los Angeles base and role in popularizing a West Coast rap wave. This regional label is accurate but broad; gangsta rap is the more defining style edge.
RILM calls Oasis the most adept exponents of Britpop; the Norwegian encyclopedia also places them among its leading acts. Central and direct fit.

The link is through Daniel Lopatin’s Chuck Person alias and *Eccojams*, a key precursor/founding work in vaporwave’s formation. Do not imply all Oneohtrix Point Never work is vaporwave; medium and alias-specific wording are appropriate.

AllMusic classifies OutKast as alternative rap; the group’s genre-crossing, experimental approach supports the label. Southern hip-hop remains the stronger regional identity, so medium is proportionate.
Rock Hall explicitly locates the duo in Southern hip-hop/Dirty South; Atlanta identity and central role make this a defining connection.

Library and musicological sources place Palestrina’s career and works in sixteenth-century Renaissance Rome. Defining composer of the period; attribution and period boundaries should be handled carefully but do not undermine this edge.
RBMA says Papa Wemba took Congo’s homegrown soukous to Europe and the world. He was a leading singer and bandleader in the style; high is warranted.

KCRW identifies her as an electroclash artist; reference classifications and contemporaneous scene histories place her among the style’s defining performers. Electroclash is a central early-career association; her later work is broader.

The Japanese pop group’s chart history and industry classification support J-pop; their more precise sound is electropop/technopop. Medium reflects a broad national-pop label rather than a defining subgenre.

Pérotin is a central figure in medieval Notre-Dame polyphony. His biography and the attribution of surviving works are uncertain because the evidence is sparse; the period association itself is secure.

Nuclear Blast directly calls Perturbator a dark-synth artist; AllMusic supports his broader synthwave identity. Dark synth is central to his project, though it remains adjacent to the wider synthwave label.
AllMusic calls them one of alternative rock’s most influential bands; the Rock Hall connects their sound to the Pacific Northwest alternative/grunge breakthrough. Direct, central association.

Scholarship and music-reference sources place Pixies in the independent/college-rock sphere and document their substantial influence on indie rock. The label is broad and their strongest conventional identity is alternative rock, so medium-high rather than unqualified high.

The band’s abrasive guitar textures and experimental recording are compatible with noise rock, and the graph’s sources link the band’s sonic innovations to the style. Noise rock is a secondary lens rather than their principal classification; keep medium.

Pizzicato Five are a defining Shibuya-kei act; Apple Music frames the group as part of the blueprint for J-pop. J-pop is a broad national/industry category, not a precise description of their eclectic sound. Medium.
A leading Latin jazz bandleader since the 1980s (Grammy winner), but a later torchbearer rather than a founding figure.

NPR places him in the New York drill scene; Complex and the New York Times document his role in taking Brooklyn drill to a wider audience. Drill is central to his signature sound, though he also recorded beyond the style.

Portishead are routinely identified with trip-hop and helped popularize the label. However, Geoff Barrow has explicitly rejected the tag; keep the useful catalog association at medium and record that this is an external genre label.

The Rock Hall describes Judas Priest as creating a mold for future heavy metal; AP says the band helped define its sound. The graph’s broad “Metal” endpoint is supported, though “heavy metal” is the more precise label.
Jamaican and international reporting identifies him as a ska pioneer and early artist-producer. His work also bridged ska, rocksteady and reggae, but ska is a defining association.

The Rock Hall explicitly includes pop among the styles Prince transformed; reference coverage calls him a pop superstar. Pop is broad, but his central influence on popular music makes the parent association secure.
His official biography calls him a bachata music idol; the Latin Grammy category and AllMusic directly support the genre. Bachata is a defining association despite his Latin pop crossovers.
Hall of Fame material and scholarship discuss Public Enemy’s politically engaged, Afrocentric rap; the group is a central example of socially conscious hip-hop. High confidence.
Public Enemy’s Long Island/New York origins and East Coast scene association are direct. Their national political impact does not weaken the regional style link.

Smithsonian catalogs performances by Purna Chandra Das within Baul songs; UNESCO documents the tradition, and his biography describes his role in broadcasting Baul music. Strong direct association; use Baul song as a culturally specific tradition, not a generic commercial genre.
The Hall of Fame calls them harbingers of hard rock; the band’s biography says it pioneered and defined the genre. Strong central association.

Scholarship explicitly analyzes Queen’s 1970s work in relation to glam rock, and reference sources identify their early glam presentation. Glam is one period/style within a broad catalog; medium is appropriate.
AllMusic places QOTSA’s emergence in the stoner-rock underground; the band later became a broader heavy-rock act. The tag is historically apt but not exhaustive, so medium.

AllMusic lists Rammstein as an industrial-metal act and describes their heavy-metal/industrial blend. The band is also commonly classified under Neue Deutsche Härte; medium reflects taxonomic overlap.

Ramones’ short, melodic, pop-inflected punk helped set the template later developed as pop-punk. They are foundationally a punk band, so treat this as a precursor/lineage association rather than their principal genre; medium.
The Rock Hall directly credits the Ramones with taking punk rock on its “maiden voyage.” Punk is central and historically defining; high is warranted.

India’s national academy recognizes him for Hindustani instrumental music; the Met describes his pivotal role in spreading Hindustani classical music internationally. The relation is direct and central.
LSO calls Reich one of minimalism’s fathers; American Mavericks calls him a founder. Canonical composer and direct central association.

AP explicitly describes early R.E.M. as alternative music; the Rock Hall traces their influence from college rock into the wider alternative breakthrough. Alternative rock is a central career identity, though the band later reached mainstream pop-rock audiences.

R.E.M.’s independent releases and college-rock origins place them in indie rock’s formative lineage. The tag is valid but broad and less defining than alternative/college rock; lower slightly from high.

Tech-house tagging exists, but stronger biographical descriptions emphasize minimal techno, microhouse and minimal house. Tech-house is a defensible adjacent classification, not his clearest central lane; medium fits.

His career as a techno DJ and producer is well established, including Detroit techno roots and influential releases. Minimal and acid techno are more precise substyles, but the parent techno edge is secure.

AllMusic describes Ride as foundational to the first shoegaze wave; the scholarly article supplies contextual corroboration. Verify/standardize the AllMusic artist URL in graph sources: the live graph uses a different Ride profile identifier.
American Mavericks ties Riley’s *In C* directly to minimalism and calls it a spiritual ancestor to later minimalist composers. Foundational relationship; high.
AllMusic names Run-D.M.C. among early New York acts; the group’s Queens origin and formative role make East Coast rap a direct fit.
Run-D.M.C. are foundational early hip-hop and fit the retrospective old-school rap period. This is a period/style label rather than their uniquely defining subgenre; medium-high is appropriate.
The Rock Hall credits Black Sabbath with bringing heavy metal into the world. The graph endpoint is the broad metal category, but heavy metal is their exact, defining association.
Real World calls them a foremost Qawwali ensemble; Radio Pakistan describes their innovations within Qawwali. Direct and central association.
The band and independent metal coverage characterize Saint Vitus as an early doom-metal band and genre pioneer. Central association; high is supported.

Oxford identifies Schoenberg as a pioneer of musical modernism. The graph’s “modern classical” label is broad and imprecise relative to modernism/atonality and the Second Viennese School; retain medium or consider a more precise genre node.
Easy Star directly calls Scientist a legendary Jamaican dub producer/engineer; AllMusic calls him a leading 1980s dub artist. Direct and central.
A conservatory-trained crossover quartet on Russian folk instruments (domra, bayan, balalaika) rather than a tradition-bearing folk ensemble.
Classic R&B vocal group; their late-1950s Leiber–Stoller records moved toward orchestrated uptown soul.
Popular from the 1970s for Russian folk songs and romances with guitar; serious-source coverage of her role is thin.
Fairuz is primarily a modern Lebanese popular singer; her repertoire is maqam-based, but she is not a classical maqam exponent in the sense of Umm Kulthum or Munir Bashir.
Concord’s biography says the band revolutionized salsa through its 1971 concert and recording at the Cheetah.

Scholarship directly names funk among the inputs synthesized into Fela’s Afrobeat, alongside highlife, jazz and Yoruba/African traditions. The component claim is strong, but do not imply funk was the only or equal source.
Historical accounts describe Fela’s transition from highlife and highlife-jazz into Afrobeat. This is a formative ingredient, not a claim that the two genres are interchangeable.
Scholarship treats Afrobeats as a broad, fluid category that intersects with hip-hop in West African scenes and global markets. Retain as cultural and stylistic exchange, not a one-way genre descent.
Krautrock is one documented electronic precursor among several; this edge does not claim sole origin.
Ambient music and chill-out culture also shape this hybrid.
Broad browsing classification only; the Latin umbrella does not imply a shared origin or erase regional and Indigenous distinctions.
Black metal is conventionally an extreme metal subgenre. A taxonomy edge is clearer than a general historical derivation; the origin story also includes early extreme-metal acts and several scenes.

Bluegrass is rooted in country and old-time string-band music; LOC calls it a new genre built on country sounds and locates it within country-and-western tradition. It is commonly treated as a country subgenre, so the current historical edge is defensible but less useful than hierarchy.

Current endpoints are blues-rock → hard rock. The hard-rock reference places blues-based rock among its formative currents, but the checked sources do not establish a clean direct descent from the named blues-rock genre. Hard rock also draws on psychedelic rock and early heavy rock; do not present this as a settled hierarchy.
One ingredient alongside rhythm and blues, country, gospel, and boogie-woogie.

The reference overview explicitly describes blues-rock as retaining blues song forms and idioms. Blues is a core component; the current `fusion_of` label is reasonable, although blues-rock is also commonly classified as a rock subgenre.

AllMusic describes blues-rock as borrowing the instrumental combo and loud amplification of rock and roll while retaining blues conventions. This supports a hybrid relation, though taxonomy also treats it as a rock subgenre.

Smithsonian history documents jazz’s incorporation of Brazilian bossa nova, while Oxford scholarship tracks bossa nova’s uptake by jazz musicians in the United States. The connection was a two-way encounter; the edge records cross-pollination rather than a parent relation.
A Brazilian tradition placed within the broad Latin umbrella for navigation.

Cambridge identifies sped-up breakbeats as foundational material for big beat and other dance genres. This supports the source direction as a rhythmic/production input, but “breakbeat” can denote a technique, sample, or broad genre; it does not establish big beat as a strict descendant of one genre.

Scholarly accounts describe breakbeat samples accelerated and reshaped into UK hardcore rave; direct rhythmic relation is strong. Medium because this is an instrumental/production practice as well as a genre label, and hardcore rave combined several other sources.

Funk breaks are a major rhythmic source for sampled breakbeats, but “breakbeat” names both a rhythmic device and several later genres. It is not sound to say the whole breakbeat genre derived from funk alone.

Supports breakbeat rhythm/sample practice feeding jungle; direction is right. Phrase the subject as breakbeat vocabulary/production, since “breakbeat” is both technique and genre family, not a sole parent.

Breakcore’s history is more commonly traced through jungle, hardcore, and drum & bass, with breakbeat hardcore a contributing predecessor rather than a sufficient parent. The existing AllMusic style page verifies breakcore but does not itself prove this direct edge.
Scene and media formation as well as sound; associated artists differed substantially.

Sources support calypso entering Jamaican mento and broader Caribbean exchange; ska’s commonly described foundations are Jamaican mento, R&B, and jazz. Direct calypso → ska is less established than a mediated influence. Existing medium confidence is generous unless note specifies the pathway.
Chillwave draws on retro 1980s synth sounds; the specific synth-pop connection is approximate and evidence does not establish direct cross-genre exchange. Low confidence.
Progressive rock drew on "classical music" broadly (often Baroque and Romantic repertoire), not specifically the 1750–1820 Classical era; only a minority of groups directly emulated it.
Blues is a major source in country music’s history; the supported direction is blues → country.
Placed under the broad Latin umbrella; cumbia has distinct Colombian roots and regional histories.

Jamaican sources describe a transition from mainstream reggae to dancehall and academic work situates dancehall’s emergence in late-1970s reggae. Dancehall also draws on sound-system, mento, and calypso traditions; medium is more appropriate than implying one-source derivation.

Thrash was one important precursor to death metal, but the latter also drew on other heavy-metal/extreme-metal currents. The edge is directionally plausible if explicitly scoped as one strand, not sole derivation.
Detroit techno is the regional form associated with the genre’s early naming and codification.
Doo-wop is commonly treated as a vocal-group branch of rhythm and blues.
Doom is a recognized heavy-metal subgenre with strong early Black Sabbath influence.

Ambient texture/approach is documented within chill-out/downbeat contexts, supporting ambient as one input to downtempo. Downtempo is a broad, heterogeneous umbrella and overlaps ambient; high overstates a single directional lineage.
Drill is a hip-hop style whose sound and context vary across local scenes.
Dub grew within reggae recording culture and remains closely related to reggae.
EDM is a broad category/umbrella, not a parent genre historically derived from house. The current direction (`EDM` derived from `house`) is inverted; house is one genre included under EDM.
Same umbrella-category error as the house edge: the academic definition explicitly lists trance among EDM genres and states EDM is a type/category, not one genre.

The electric bass was designed as a portable, amplified alternative to the upright/double bass and retained its tuning/register function, but is a distinct fretted instrument. Keep only with this design-ancestry qualification.

Electric guitar is a guitar form whose amplified pickup changes sound production and performance context. Derivation is reasonable, but it is not merely an acoustic guitar with amplification; construction and playing practices diversified.

“Electric piano” covers electro-mechanical instruments such as Rhodes/Wurlitzer with different sound-producing mechanisms, as well as electric amplification variants. Retain ancestry only with a note that the label spans distinct mechanisms, not a uniform piano subtype.

The scholarly sources confirm electro house as a recognized house subgenre, but the accessible evidence does not establish electro itself as a co-equal parent. The sound label often refers to electro-style timbres within house; treat this as a stylistic component, not a proven two-parent genre origin.

House is the clear parent tradition: a sociology study explicitly lists electro house as a house subgenre. The `fusion_of` edge captures house as an ingredient but `subgenre_of` would be taxonomically more exact if the graph permits one relation per pair.
Electroclash drew on Detroit electro and related electronic dance styles while combining them with new wave, punk and synth-pop. Strong as one component, not a complete account of the genre.
Scholarship and contemporary coverage identify synth-pop among electroclash’s sources, alongside new wave, punk, techno and electro. Well supported as a component.

Early emo/“emocore” formed in the 1980s Washington, DC hardcore scene. Broad punk-rock ancestry is true but less specific; use hardcore punk as the source endpoint if the graph contains it, and avoid collapsing later indie, pop, and post-hardcore waves into one lineage.
The folk revival and blues shared repertory, performers and audiences, especially in the mid-century revival circuit.

Scholarly discussion directly identifies disco sampling as important to French Touch/French house. Direction is strong; keep medium because disco is one among funk, house, and studio/production inputs.

House is a clear musical and production source for French Touch. “French Touch” is a scene/umbrella with varied styles rather than one sharply bounded genre, so medium and the current scope note are apt.
Funk elements entered fusion in the early 1970s (e.g. Headhunters); jazz and rock remain the core components.

Scholarship describes G-funk as an identifiable West Coast rap subgenre, while AllMusic documents its signature production and early-1990s prominence. Direction is right: G-funk is the narrower regional style.
Documented influence on particular composers and works; not a general ancestry claim.

Supports influence of Balinese gamelan on particular minimalist composers, notably structural/rhythmic ideas. This is not a claim that gamelan shaped minimalism as a whole; medium is suitable with specific-composers caveat.

Oxford explicitly calls gangsta rap a subgenre emerging from hip-hop/rap, especially in Southern California. It is a recognized hip-hop subgenre, though the label has expanded beyond that initial region.
AllMusic defines garage rock as a raw form of rock & roll. The endpoint and direction are appropriate.

The category spans pop, R&B, and rock & roll and often describes a gendered vocal-group format, production system, and historical market category as much as one coherent sound. Pop is a defensible broad parent, but the edge should not imply a uniform musical subgenre.
Rock and roll is one influence on glam rock alongside bubblegum pop, art rock, and theatrical performance; it is not the genre’s sole parent.

Music scholarship traces “gothic/goth” as a label for post-punk bands and describes the scene’s roots in punk/post-punk. Gothic rock is a recognized branch within the wider, fragmented post-punk field.

Gqom is described as a variant of South African house, but scholarship also stresses its post-kwaito lineage and distinct self-definition. Keep the parent edge at medium with Durban/South African context; it is not merely another generic house subtype.

UK garage is identified as a precursor and grime is linked to London’s garage scene, but grime also draws from jungle, dancehall, hip-hop, and sound-system culture. The existing derivation is plausible if qualified as a major lineage rather than a single source.
Grunge is widely classified within alternative rock. Its punk and metal roots and eventual mainstream commercial identity make it a specific branch, not a synonym for all alternative rock.
Hard rock is a type/style of rock music. This broad parent relation is valid, despite fuzzy borders with heavy metal and blues rock.
Hardstyle incorporated hard-trance and hardcore influences; this is a broad lineage summary, not an exclusive origin.
Hardstyle incorporated hard-trance and hardcore influences; this is a broad lineage summary, not an exclusive origin.
Jazz swing and performance practices influenced Ghanaian highlife bands; the supported direction is jazz → highlife.

Documents Indian/Hindustani concepts and musicians influencing particular jazz artists and currents. Direction is valid as exchange/influence, but edge must not generalize to all jazz. Existing caveat and medium score are appropriate.

Editorial discography and scholarship treat horrorcore as a rap/hip-hop subgenre shaped by horror themes and hip-hop beats. Boundaries overlap with gangsta and hardcore rap, so medium-high is more appropriate than an absolute taxonomy.

House inherited and reworked disco records and DJ practices, but it became a distinct Chicago sound and social culture. Keep the derivation edge as historical lineage, not as a claim that house is simply electronic disco.
Sources identify hyphy as a Bay Area rap/hip-hop subgenre and movement within West Coast hip-hop. It is a regional branch and culture, not a separate genre unrelated to West Coast rap.

Impressionism is a late-19th/early-20th-century classical movement and an important precursor/part of early modernist music, but it is not always treated as a “subgenre” of modern classical. Keep at medium as a period/style taxonomy; consider a movement or stylistic-lineage relation if the schema supports it.

Industrial metal uses heavy-metal riffs and is treated within metal taxonomies, but key accounts describe it as a hybrid of industrial dance, metal, and hardcore punk. The heavy-metal parent is defensible at medium confidence, with the hybrid nature stated.

J-pop is a broad, market and cultural label for Japanese mainstream popular music spanning multiple sounds, rather than a narrow style nested neatly inside Anglo-American pop. A broad pop parent is reasonable; use medium confidence and avoid treating the labels as interchangeable.
Jazz reaches deep house mainly through 1980s jazz-funk/fusion harmony; Larry Heard drummed in jazz-fusion bands.
Institutional history and scholarship directly define the style through rap/hip-hop practice with jazz musicians, samples and improvisation. Hip-hop is an essential component.
The sources document jazz instrumentation, improvisation, repertoire and samples as core to jazz-rap. The fusion claim is direct; individual tracks vary in how much live jazz they contain.

K-pop is Korean popular music oriented toward global audiences and blends many genres; scholarship distinguishes it from all popular music made in Korea. It belongs under broad pop, but the parent is a cultural umbrella more than a single musical formula.
Krautrock is treated here as a West German branch of experimental rock; several groups also moved toward electronic music.
House was a major influence that kwaito localized alongside South African musical practices; this does not reduce kwaito to a house subgenre.

Math rock emerged within the 1990s alternative-rock landscape and has links to indie and post-rock, but scholarship describes it as a specific, internationally used category with roots beyond indie. The current indie-rock parent is plausible in some scenes, not universal; consider a broader rock parent or keep only at low-medium confidence.

Chronological transition and inherited practices are clear, but “medieval” and “Renaissance” are period labels, not discrete agents. The medium influence rating treats an era boundary as a directed causal edge; use derivation/continuity language instead.
Merengue is a Dominican musical tradition and regional Latin American style. `Latin` is a broad geographic/catalog umbrella, not a precise musical parent. Keep at medium and state the umbrella sense.
Academic source describes grunge as an amalgam of punk and metal styles in late-1980s Seattle. Supports heavy-metal influence as one component; medium correctly avoids a one-parent account.

Heavy metal emerged from overlapping blues-rock, psychedelic rock, and hard-rock currents; its boundary from hard rock is historically disputed. The current high-level taxonomy conflates a predecessor with an adjacent classification, so keep only as qualified low-medium ancestry or replace with influences.

Metalcore is commonly filed under heavy metal, but its defining hybrid formation includes hardcore punk and multiple metal strands. A broad subtype edge is defensible; it should not imply a simple one-parent genealogy.

Some Krautrock artists intersected with American avant-garde/minimalist ideas, but the source frames a specific contested connection; repetitive texture alone is not proof of influence. Generic genre-to-genre causal edge at medium is too broad.

Minimalism is a compositional movement in art/contemporary classical music, but also appears in popular and electronic music. `modern-classical` is a useful broad parent for this graph, not an exclusive taxonomy. Medium.
The Minimoog translated modular-synth concepts into a compact fixed-configuration instrument; it was not itself modular.
Grove defines modal jazz as a style of jazz; RILM and Jazz at Lincoln Center likewise describe it as a jazz style/movement. The hierarchy is direct.

The present direction is theremin → modular synthesizer. Sources support Moog’s early theremin work and subsequent synthesizer development, but not a strong causal design lineage from theremin technology to modular synthesis. Reframe as Moog’s career/instrument-making influence and lower confidence.

Neo-soul developed in a contemporary R&B environment shaped by hip-hop, with hip-hop rhythm and production influencing some artists. Soul revival and live instrumentation are more defining; medium is appropriate and the edge should not imply equal fusion across all neo-soul.
The return to classic soul performance, songwriting and sound is central to neo-soul’s formation. This is a defining component, though neo-soul remains a broad and debated marketing/category label.
Carnegie Hall and the music-industry genre standard describe hip-hop drum production/techniques as a defining ingredient, combined with R&B vocal and songwriting approaches. Strong support.

New jack swing retains contemporary R&B songwriting and vocal style while incorporating hip-hop production. Strong component relation; the graph should avoid suggesting R&B is a minor or optional ingredient.
New wave emerged in punk’s wake and in punk’s image, then broadened toward more pop-oriented and electronic forms; it shared scenes and personnel with punk.

Nu metal draws on heavy metal but is also commonly placed within alternative metal and its own status as an accepted metal subgenre has been contested. The current parent is overbroad; retain only low-medium until the graph offers an `alternative-metal` parent or note that the taxonomy is umbrella-level.
Old-school rap is an early historical/style subset of hip-hop, though period boundaries and the distinction between rap music and hip-hop culture vary. Keep medium and preserve the period sense.
Cristofori developed the piano from the harpsichord maker’s craft and keyboard instrument, replacing plucked jacks with hammer action; the piano is a distinct invention, not a harpsichord subtype.
Pop-punk combines punk’s speed/attitude with pop melody and is routinely classified within the punk-rock family. Taxonomies vary, but the child-to-parent direction is sound.

Historical accounts describe rock and roll as a cross-pollination of blues, country, gospel, Latin, and pop traditions; “pop” is also a broad commercial category, so this link should not be read as a narrow one-way genre influence.
Soul crossed into and helped shape the mainstream pop market; this edge records that crossover.
Post-hardcore emerged from hardcore punk, itself a punk-rock branch, and broadened its musical expression. The graph lacks a hardcore-punk endpoint, so this is a coarse parent link.

Post-punk is documented as a formative strand for later alternative/indie rock, especially through scenes and bands. “Alternative rock” is a broad umbrella that can itself include post-punk; medium and a non-exclusive lineage caveat are appropriate.
Post-punk followed punk and developed partly from it, but its boundaries are contested and its influences extend well beyond punk.

Bristol artists drew on post-punk alongside dub/reggae sound systems and hip-hop. Good support for a strand of influence, but genre label is contested and trip-hop is multi-source; high overstates the edge.
Psytrance developed in Goa trance/psychedelic dance contexts; Goa is the more specific immediate antecedent, so generic trance is a broad parent.
Oxford explicitly identifies punk and metal as ingredients in grunge. Direction is supported; medium is appropriate because Seattle grunge synthesized multiple inputs and local scenes.
Punk rock is an offshoot of rock music and is commonly treated as a rock subgenre. High confidence.

Cambridge documents Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan’s qawwali being embraced by rock musicians and his collaboration with Western pop styles; scholarship on qawwali in diaspora discusses its transformations. Keep as a performer-mediated cross-cultural encounter, not a blanket claim that rock derives from qawwali.
Blues is a major antecedent of R&B alongside gospel, jazz and other practices; this is not a single-source derivation.
Reggae followed rocksteady and ska; rocksteady is one important antecedent, not the sole source.

Scholarship and LOC describe hip-hop/rap as a major strand of reggaeton’s formation. It also incorporates Puerto Rican, Panamanian and Jamaican dancehall/reggae traditions; this is not “Latin hip-hop” alone.

Reggae en español and Jamaican dancehall are important roots, but the latter is a more precise lineage than generic reggae. Keep medium and note the Panamanian/Jamaican pathways and hip-hop influence.

Musicological treatments describe gradual, overlapping transition and changing currents around 1600. This is continuity/period succession rather than evidence of a single influence from one bounded genre to another; medium should not imply a clean causal line.
Rocksteady developed out of Jamaican ska in the mid-1960s.

Modern style retains/extends some Romantic techniques while modernism also reacts against Romantic conventions; music historiography cautions that period labels and transitions are problematic. Current note captures the two-way relationship, but graph edge is one-way and “modern classical” spans many incompatible strands.
Salsa is widely cataloged as Latin music, but `Latin` is a geographic/industry umbrella and salsa formed through transnational Afro-Caribbean exchange. Medium, with umbrella caveat.
Cuban son is one foundational ancestor of salsa, alongside other Cuban and Caribbean forms; this is not an exclusive derivation.

Adolphe Sax experimented by fitting a bass-clarinet mouthpiece to an ophicleide; this clarinet-derived single-reed idea contributed to the saxophone, alongside a new brass body and bore. This is a design influence, not a claim that the saxophone descends from the clarinet alone.
Shoegaze is a rock subgenre and is strongly associated with indie-rock scenes and labels. It also overlaps with noise-pop and dream-pop; indie-rock is a defensible, if not exclusive, parent.

Sources describe soca as a revisioning or evolution of calypso; early experiments also incorporated East Indian rhythmic elements, without making soca a simple two-parent fusion.
RBMA identifies Lord Shorty/Ras Shorty I as a soca pioneer and links his 1973 “Indrani” to the genre’s early development; Caribbean Beat presents the origin story as involving multiple contributors.
Caribbean Beat describes Montano as a soca star and later as the genre’s biggest superstar, supporting representative status.

Caribbean Beat identifies Calypso Rose as a calypso icon who joined Soca and names her 1977 recording “Give More Tempo.” This supports her early representative role, though the reviewed article does not document a direct influence on later artists.
